subject: making
must_answer: Soap, lime, cement, glass, charcoal, dyes, fertiliser, disinfectants
notes: Checked 21 Nov 2026 by reading inside the ZIMs. Soap: VITA Home Soap Making (CD3WD, T2-015, core) is the family-scale guide (commercial lye or lye leached from wood ash; gloves, eye protection, lye into water never water into lye). Its first aid for lye is out of date: on skin or in the eyes, rinse with plenty of running water for at least 15-20 minutes (no vinegar); if swallowed, rinse the mouth, do not make the person vomit, no vinegar or citrus, get medical help. GTZ How to Make? An Improved Soap (1993) and CDI Soap Production (1995), both in CD3WD, are small-business depth. Lime: GTZ Small Scale Production of Lime for Building (1985, CD3WD) is project planning and kilns, with no burn warnings: quicklime and slaking burn skin and eyes, so wear goggles and gloves. Cement, bricks, kilns: CD3WD (GTZ, ILO). Pottery: GTZ Self-Reliant Potter books (CD3WD); Glazes (1993) warns that lead glazes are poisonous and gives lead-free ones. Charcoal: T2-124. Chemistry: LibreTexts (T3-014). Gutenberg technology set (T3-031, standard): soap-making manuals, glass manufacture, Henley's formulas; industrial and pre-1930, reference only (some recipes use lead, arsenic or mercury). Still missing: glass making at household scale (none exists; glass needs a furnace at about 1,400-1,500 C).
